config.title: CSS custom properties in JS

intro.title: CSS custom properties in JS
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple interactive webpage where you can change the color and size of a box using JavaScript. You will learn how to use CSS custom properties (also called CSS variables) to store values like colors and sizes, and then update them dynamically with JavaScript. The main technologies involved are CSS for styling and defining the custom properties, and JavaScript for accessing and modifying them. This will help you understand how to make your web pages more dynamic and responsive to user interactions.
intro.usecase: CSS custom properties in JavaScript are essential for creating dynamic, theme-aware interfaces that respond to user interactions. In real applications, this pattern powers live theme switchers in dashboards like analytics tools, where users toggle between light/dark modes and see immediate visual updates. Developers use this technique for interactive UI components like adjustable panels with resizable widths, real-time form validation with color-coded feedback, and dynamic data visualizations that change colors based on data thresholds. This approach separates styling logic from JavaScript while maintaining runtime control over visual properties.

objectives: Initialize CSS custom properties in a JavaScript file to define dynamic styling variables.
Apply CSS custom properties to HTML elements using JavaScript to control visual presentation.
Manipulate CSS custom property values through JavaScript functions to update styles in real-time.
Integrate CSS custom properties with JavaScript event handlers to create interactive UI changes.
Construct a responsive color scheme by binding CSS custom properties to user input controls.
Configure CSS custom properties to dynamically adjust layout properties based on JavaScript logic.
Update CSS custom properties across multiple elements simultaneously using JavaScript loops or selectors.

steps.instruction: Create a CSS file and define custom properties using the --prefix syntax. Add a :root selector with at least two custom properties.
steps.hint: Use the :root pseudo-class to define global custom properties. Start each property name with two hyphens (--).

steps.title: Apply custom properties to elements
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for a paragraph element that sets its color using the var() function with your custom property name.
steps.hint: Use the selector 'p' and the property 'color' with var(--your-property-name).
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS rule for paragraphs that uses var() to apply a custom property value.
successCriteria: The CSS contains a 'p' selector with a 'color' property using var(--your-property-name).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using the var() function with your custom property name inside the 'p' rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you added a CSS rule for 'p' with 'color: var(--your-property-name);'.

steps.title: Create HTML structure with CSS classes
steps.instruction: Create a <div> element with the class 'container' that will wrap your content.
steps.hint: Add a <div> tag with class='container' after your existing CSS rules.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS rule for a .container class is added to your stylesheet.
successCriteria: The .container class selector exists in the CSS file.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a .container class selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. You need to create a CSS rule for a .container class.

steps.title: Link CSS file to HTML document
steps.instruction: Add a link element inside the HTML head section to connect your CSS file. The link should have rel="stylesheet" and href="styles.css".
steps.hint: Use the <link> tag with the correct attributes to link an external CSS file.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Linking an external CSS file -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
steps.expectedOutcome: The CSS file is properly linked to the HTML document, allowing styles to be applied.
successCriteria: A link element with rel="stylesheet" and href="styles.css" is added to the HTML head section.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your link element has both rel="stylesheet" and href="styles.css" attributes.
steps.feedbackWrong: The link element is missing or incorrect. Check that you're using the <link> tag with the proper attributes to connect the CSS file.

steps.hint: In your HTML file, add a <script> element with a src attribute pointing to 'script.js'. The script tag should be placed before the closing </body> tag.

steps.title: Access CSS custom properties in JavaScript
steps.instruction: In your JavaScript file, write a function named readCustomProperty that uses getComputedStyle() to read the value of a CSS custom property from an element.
steps.hint: You can use getComputedStyle(element).getPropertyValue('--property-name') to retrieve the value of a custom property.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named readCustomProperty is created that accesses a CSS custom property value using getComputedStyle().
successCriteria: The function readCustomProperty is defined and uses getComputedStyle() with getPropertyValue() to read a CSS custom property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function uses getComputedStyle() and getPropertyValue() to access the custom property value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function doesn't properly access CSS custom properties. Review how to use getComputedStyle() and getPropertyValue().

steps.title: Wire JavaScript functions to controls
steps.instruction: Add an event listener to the button element that calls the updateColor function when clicked.
steps.hint: Use addEventListener with 'click' event type and pass the updateColor function as the callback.
steps.seedCode:
<!-- Add your HTML structure here -->

<!-- Add a button element below -->
<button id="colorButton">Change Color</button>

<script>
// Access CSS custom properties in JavaScript
const root = document.documentElement;

// Modify custom properties with JavaScript
function updateColor() {
  root.style.setProperty('--main-color', '#ff5733');
}

// Add event listener to button
</script>
steps.expectedOutcome: The button will trigger the updateColor function when clicked, changing the CSS custom property value.
successCriteria: Button has a click event listener that calls the updateColor function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're adding the event listener to the button with id 'colorButton' and calling updateColor as the callback.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button isn't properly wired. Check that you're using addEventListener with 'click' event and the updateColor function.
